name: Kelewele
summary: Cubes of ripe plantain marinated in ginger, chilli and spices, fried until sticky, sweet and crisp-edged.
story: Kelewele is a popular Ghanaian street snack, sold in the evenings from roadside stands, often served in paper with roasted peanuts. It is made from very ripe plantain and a warming ginger-pepper spice mix.

steps.title: Cut the plantain
steps.text: Cut the peeled plantains into 2 cm cubes or thick diagonal slices. Very ripe plantain is soft, so use a sharp knife.

steps.title: Make the spice paste
steps.text: Mash together the ginger, garlic, onion, cayenne, cloves, nutmeg and salt with 1 tablespoon of water into a thick paste.

steps.title: Coat the plantain
steps.text: Toss the plantain gently in the paste until each piece is evenly coated. Leave to marinate for 10-15 minutes.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat the oil to about 170 C (340 F). Test with a cube: it should sizzle immediately and bubble steadily.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Fry in small batches for 3-4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden brown with dark caramelised edges. Do not crowd the pan because the sugar burns quickly.

steps.title: Drain and serve
steps.text: Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve hot with roasted peanuts.

tips: Choose plantains that are almost black; green or just yellow ones turn starchy rather than sweet.
Medium heat is key because the sugars in the fruit burn fast.
Eat straight away for the best crispy edges.
Add a squeeze of lime for brightness if you like.

swaps.swap: A pinch of allspice or mixed spice replaces both.
Toss with 2 tbsp oil and bake at 220 C (425 F) for 20-25 minutes, turning once; less crisp but lighter.
